\begin{lemma}[Register bounds imply a valid guard]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.preS_A}
\difficulty{1}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Boolean-valued function on four indices
and finite Boolean words, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean word. If all eighteen
registers of a state $\mathrm{st}$ are at most $B$, then for every label $\ell$ the
abstract configuration with label $\ell$, register values given by $\mathrm{st}$, and no
answer satisfies the guard for the program $A_E$ and input $x$: its registers are
bounded by $B$, and its instruction satisfies the guard precondition.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reachability from a predecessor configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices
and each Boolean word, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Let $\mathrm{st}$ be an
18-register machine state, $\ell$ a machine label, and $c$ an abstract configuration. If
every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$, and there is a finite run from the
configuration obtained by taking one machine step from label $\ell$ with register values
given by $\mathrm{st}$ to $c$, with every configuration strictly before its endpoint
satisfying the guard with bound $B$, then there is also a finite run from the original
configuration at label $\ell$ with those register values to $c$, with every
configuration strictly before its endpoint satisfying the same guard.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reachability from Equal Register States]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cont}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cont}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV}
\difficulty{1}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let
$\mathrm{orc}\colon\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an
oracle, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $l$ be a label of the program $A(E)$.
If register states $\mathrm{st}$ and $\mathrm{st}'$ are equal, then every configuration
reachable in finitely many steps from label $l$ with the register vector of
$\mathrm{st}'$ and no answer, with each earlier configuration satisfying the program’s
safety condition and all register values at most $B$, is also reachable under those same
conditions from label $l$ with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting from Equal Register States]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.contH}

\difficulty{1}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let
$\mathrm{orc}\colon\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an

If register states $\mathrm{st}$ and $\mathrm{st}'$ are equal and the machine started at
label $l$ with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}'$ and no answer halts with answer
$r\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ after finitely many steps, with every earlier
configuration satisfying the program’s safety condition and all register values at most
$B$, then it also halts with answer $r$ from label $l$ with the register vector of
$\mathrm{st}$ and no answer, under those same conditions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Execution of the Endpoint-Stack Pop Routine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pop_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pop_run}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cp_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.hv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.sb_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.shReg, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.sh_run, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}

Let $E$ and $B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each
of four decider indices and Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $b$ be a
Boolean phase. For a machine register state $st$, suppose its loop counter, time scratch
register, copy-and-shift scratch register, pop scratch register, and popped-endpoint
register are all zero; every register is at most $B$; and its saved-endpoints stack has
value $q2^{st.w}+e$, where $q,e$ are natural numbers and $e<2^{st.w}$. Starting with
state $st$, no recorded answer, and the instruction that begins popping the saved
endpoint for phase $b$, the abstract machine reaches the instruction that increments the

register changed to $e$, all other registers unchanged, and no answer recorded. Every
configuration before the final one satisfies the program guard with bound $B$.
\end{theorem}
